clue.text: Sequence of command

definitions.meaning: an arrangement in which one thing follows another in set succession
an instruction given with authority, as by an officer

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a set arrangement of items in succession and an authoritative instruction that must be obeyed.

clue.text: Just comparatively varied if rare

indicators.note: varied says the letters of the two words beside it are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone muses that what is unusual turns out, by comparison, to be more equitable.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of an adjective meaning just or equitable, so 'more just'.

clue.text: Last of the lot, in spite of everything

definitions.meaning: coming when every other one has had its turn, at the very end
nevertheless, regardless of what has gone before

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means coming behind every other one, and idiomatically means nevertheless or regardless.

clue.text: Put it down to a professional writer

parts.note: a scribe is a clerk or copyist who writes for a living

explanation.surface: A remark that some piece of writing should be credited to a hired penman.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute something to a cause or author is to credit it or put it down to them.

clue.text: Sharing party Kate Parr arranged

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the two names are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Henry VIII's last queen, Katherine Parr, organises a party for all to share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges KATE and PARR together. Katherine Parr was the sixth wife of England's Henry VIII.
explanation.definitionFit: One who takes a share in something, such as a meal, is a participant or sharing party.

clue.text: Source of timber for the aircraft industry?

definitions.text: Source of timber for the aircraft industry?

parts.words: Source of timber for the aircraft industry?
parts.note: an aircraft is also called an aeroplane, so a timber source for that industry would be its own kind of tree; really it is a broad-leaved shade tree common in city streets

explanation.definitionFit: A tall broad-leaved tree yielding timber, whose first word also means an aeroplane.

clue.text: Where Holmes booked the Professor and the Autocrat

definitions.text: Where Holmes booked the Professor and the Autocrat

parts.words: Where Holmes booked the Professor and the Autocrat
parts.note: the American writer Oliver Wendell Holmes wrote books titled for the Autocrat and the Professor seated at a morning meal piece of furniture

explanation.walkthrough: Not Sherlock Holmes: Oliver Wendell Holmes wrote The Autocrat of the Breakfast-Table and The Professor at the Breakfast-Table, so 'booked' means put into a book title.
explanation.definitionFit: The two book titles name the morning-meal furniture as the setting for these talkative characters.

clue.text: See 7
Truthful Roman girl in overalls

indicators.note: in says the name sits inside the letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An honest young Roman woman is dressed in overalls.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl's name sits inside 'overalls'. It is also the Latin feminine of verus, 'true', hence 'Truthful Roman'.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name which in Latin is the feminine form of the word for true.

clue.text: Doubly expensive expression of regret

indicators.note: doubly says the word for expensive is written two times over

parts.note: something dear costs a lot

explanation.surface: A sigh over something that cost twice too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild exclamation of dismay or sorrow, like 'oh my' or 'alas'.

clue.text: Area of a former camper's pitch

parts.note: ex- is a prefix for former, as in ex-wife
a camper pitches a tent

explanation.surface: Asking how much ground an ex-camper once pitched on covered.
explanation.definitionFit: Scope or size of a region, how far something stretches.

clue.text: In favour of a Malaysian craft

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone backs a boat from Malaysia.
explanation.walkthrough: A proa (or prau) is a fast sailing boat with an outrigger, used in the Malay archipelago.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malay outrigger sailing boat, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Second-rate swindles in parentheses

parts.note: B is a grade below A, so second-rate
rackets are dishonest schemes or scams

explanation.surface: Inferior frauds are mentioned as an aside, in parentheses.
explanation.definitionFit: Round or square marks enclosing words, here as a synonym of the round ones.

clue.text: The auditor's instruction to the shoplifter?

definitions.text: The auditor's instruction to the shoplifter?

parts.words: The auditor's instruction to the shoplifter?
parts.note: an accountant counting goods tells staff to make an inventory; said to a thief it would be an invitation to steal the merchandise

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to make an inventory or reassess, but literally it means to remove goods.

clue.text: Spoils in the manner of Sicilian wine

parts.note: mars means spoils or damages
a la is French-derived for in the style of

explanation.surface: A wine from Sicily is ruined, done in a certain style.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine made around a port in western Sicily.

clue.text: Stifles Mum, held by Nazi police

indicators.note: held by says the word for mum is gripped inside the letters for the police

parts.note: the SS was the paramilitary police force of Nazi Germany
mum is a mother

explanation.surface: A mother arrested by the SS has her voice stifled.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffocates or suppresses, as a fire is put out by cutting off its air.

clue.text: Cross-country runner who is a worrier

definitions.meaning: an athlete who runs cross-country races, named after hounds used in hare hunting
one who harasses or pesters, as a dog worries sheep

explanation.definitionFit: Both a club cross-country athlete and one who harries or keeps attacking.

clue.text: So long in France!

parts.note: what a French speaker says when parting, the equivalent of goodbye or see you

explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for goodbye, literally 'until seeing again'.

clue.text: What the well-dressed barrister takes on

definitions.text: What the well-dressed barrister takes on

parts.words: What the well-dressed barrister takes on
parts.note: a smart dresser takes on fresh clothes; a lawyer takes on a fresh case in court

explanation.walkthrough: A barrister is a British trial lawyer; 'suit' is both clothes and a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a freshly bought set of clothes and a fresh lawsuit or legal action.

clue.text: Verse about one Italian artist

indicators.note: about says the word verse goes around the word one

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A line of poetry written about a single painter from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Verse' looks like part of the picture, but it is the outer piece. Paolo Veronese was a sixteenth-century Venetian painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paolo Veronese, a Renaissance painter of the Venetian school.

clue.text: Formerly part of another story

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something that happened before belongs to a different tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word meaning once, in the past, as in its longer form erstwhile.

clue.text: Part otherwise absorbed

indicators.note: otherwise says the letters of the word beside it are set in another order

explanation.surface: An actor's role, played another way, is engrossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Engrossed or wholly engaged, as in being entranced.

clue.text: Brown ale for the baggage bearer

definitions.meaning: a dark brown beer brewed from charred malt
a person employed to carry luggage at a station or hotel

explanation.definitionFit: Both a dark beer once favoured by London market workers and a person who carries luggage.

clue.text: Bed for those who need to a count sheep

definitions.text: Bed for those who need to a count sheep

parts.words: Bed for those who need to a count sheep
parts.note: a mattress stuffed with wool waste, and the word also means a group of sheep, the thing insomniacs count

explanation.definitionFit: Wool tufts used to stuff mattresses, and also a herd of sheep.

clue.text: Pitches less quietly — therefore is scratched?

indicators.note: less says a letter is taken away from the word pitches

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A football pitch grows quieter, so its turf gets scuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing P (piano, quietly) from 'Pitches'; the definition says what an itchy spot causes: it is scratched.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritations of the skin, and something that tingles is what one scratches.

clue.text: Rigorously cut off city of the former isle

parts.note: to sever is to cut off
Ely is a cathedral city in the old Isle of Ely, a former English county

explanation.surface: Someone banished harshly from a city on an island that no longer exists.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Ely, in the fens of eastern England, was a county until 1965.
explanation.definitionFit: Strictly or harshly, with stern exactness.

clue.text: Points gained from scratch

definitions.meaning: the tally of points made in a game
to mark a surface with a cut line or groove

explanation.definitionFit: Both the tally in a game and a cut line marked on a surface.

clue.text: Persistent effort by which French passengers were moved

definitions.text: by which French passengers were moved
definitions.meaning: a French public stagecoach of past centuries

explanation.definitionFit: Both careful, steady hard work and an old French public stagecoach.
